clue.text: Seeing somebody more than once perhaps, one is bound to go dizzy with love

definitions.text: Seeing somebody more than once perhaps

indicators.note: going dizzy means the letters spin into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in love is certain to feel giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go dizzy' shuffles I (one), IS, BOUND and LOVE together. 'Seeing somebody' suggests dating, but here it means seeing literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplopia, the visual disorder, makes a single object or person appear twice, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Traveller may be found here dead, having unfortunately capsized with the top of her arm trapped

indicators.note: trapped means the following pieces are held inside the others
a boat that has capsized is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim report of someone who drowned when a boat overturned, her arm caught underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' reads a word bottom to top in a down clue. The sad overturning looks literal but signals the reversal; 'the top of her' is just H.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a dharmsala is a rest house for pilgrims and travellers.

clue.text: Educational establishment's head of teaching introduced modules

indicators.note: introduced means one piece is brought into the middle of the other

parts.note: a university is an educational establishment, shortened to uni; with the possessive it gives UNI'S

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A college's head of teaching has brought in a modular course structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' puts T, the first letter of 'teaching', inside UNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses are split into units, the separate parts or blocks of study also called modules.

clue.text: I'm thinking you should stop blocking the view!

definitions.meaning: a stalling phrase used while pondering a question

definitions.text: you should stop blocking the view!
definitions.meaning: a literal request to be allowed to see past someone

explanation.surface: Someone mulling a problem while snapping at a person standing in their way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a pause for thought and, read literally, a plea to be allowed a look.

clue.text: Tubby guy employed as a tax inspector?

parts.note: read as 'tub-y', of a tub: a vat is a large tub
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A portly fellow working as a taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tubby' looks like 'fat' but is read as relating to a tub, a VAT. VAT is the UK's value added tax, collected by HM Revenue and Customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British name for an official of the value added tax office, a kind of tax inspector.

clue.text: Thrilled to embrace New Age feeling

indicators.note: to embrace means to wrap around the following pieces

parts.note: to be sent is old slang for being thrilled or carried away
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone excited to take up New Age thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' looks like the spiritual movement, but splits into two separate pieces; the container wraps them inside the word for thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, so it is a synonym for a feeling.

clue.text: A little bird heading north without hindrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A small bird flying north with nothing in its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns WO into OW. The phrase 'without let or hindrance' is a legal formula found in British passports.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so it is literally a little bird.

clue.text: Unfinished track cut by a popular backing musician …

indicators.note: cut by means the first part is split open by the second
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a piste is a ski run or track

indicators.note: backing means the word is reversed

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A musician playing behind a popular song that has been edited short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing musician' wants to be one phrase, but 'backing' belongs to the wordplay as the reversal signal. The ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is a musician who plays the piano.

clue.text: Arrange temp repairs for a sandwich shop

indicators.note: repairs means the letters are mended into a new order

explanation.surface: Booking a temporary worker to fix up a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'repairs' does the work. Pret A Manger is a UK chain of sandwich shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Pret A Manger is a high street chain known for its ready-made sandwiches.

clue.text: … who has a number one?

parts.note: a number one is childish slang for a wee, also called a tinkle; following the pianist clue, it also suggests someone who plays the keys lightly

explanation.surface: Continuing from the pianist: a performer with a chart-topping hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the musician, so 'number one' suggests a hit record; it is nursery slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tinkles is either a child having a wee or someone lightly playing a piano.

clue.text: Messy diners ought to sit up front

indicators.note: messy means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Untidy restaurant customers ought to be seated at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take the passenger seat beside the driver of a car.

clue.text: Attempt to avoid correspondence about awards

indicators.note: about means the result is turned round
to avoid means the following word is left out of the other

parts.note: symmetry is the correspondence of parts on either side of a line
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone trying to dodge the post about prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' looks like letters but means SYMMETRY; 'to avoid' removes TRY, leaving SYMME, which 'about' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmys are the American television industry's annual prizes.

clue.text: I reached over and devoured a little bit of duck without much meat on the bone

definitions.text: without much meat on the bone

indicators.note: over means the preceding pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: came means arrived or reached
ate means devoured

indicators.note: a little bit of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner leans across and wolfs down a scrap of duck that was mostly bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns I plus CAME into EMACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, the idiom 'without much meat on the bone' describing a skinny body.

clue.text: Legendary nurse in a bad French hospital starts to earn accolades — about time!

indicators.note: about means the preceding pieces wrap around the next one

parts.note: mal is French for bad
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A nurse in a poor French hospital at last starts to win praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time!' reads as an exclamation of relief, but signals the container: the time abbreviation sits inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Amalthea was the goat or nymph who suckled the infant Zeus, so a nurse from legend.

clue.text: This endless, endless sportscast initially excluded Balding

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off
excluded means that letter is taken out

parts.note: endless means nonstop, going on without a break

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sports broadcast that dropped Clare Balding, the BBC presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This endless' gives THI; the second 'endless' is NONSTOP, and 'excluded' drops S, the first letter of 'sportscast'. Balding looks like the presenter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin on top is the idiom for losing one's hair, i.e. going bald.

clue.text: Bread baked without yeast in the middle is rubbish

indicators.note: baked means the remaining letters are cooked into a new shape
without means that letter is removed
in the middle picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Unleavened bread is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A, the middle of 'yeast', leaving BRED; 'baked' rearranges it to DEBR.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or wreckage, the remains of something broken.

clue.text: Spiteful wartime general striking France, Romania and America

indicators.note: striking means crossing out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: General Franco led the Nationalists in the Spanish Civil War
F is the international vehicle code for France
RO is the international code for Romania

explanation.surface: A vindictive wartime commander attacking three nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like attacking but means deleting: F comes off FRANCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of bitter resentment, which is what spiteful means.

clue.text: Lower part of the Congo possibly was passed over by migrating weaver birds

definitions.text: Lower part of the Congo possibly

indicators.note: passed over means the word was is left out of the letters
migrating means the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A flock of weaver birds flying over the lower Congo region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'migrating' rearranges WEAVER BIRDS, and 'passed over by' leaves out the letters of WAS. 'Lower part of the Congo' reads as geography but means its bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed is the bottom of a river, so the lowest part of the Congo river.

clue.text: Cab drivers admit an inability to coordinate

indicators.note: admit means let the following word inside

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British drivers' organisation
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Taxi drivers confess they are clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cab drivers' reads as one phrase but splits in two, the drivers being the British motoring organisation holding the cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is the medical term for loss of control of bodily movements.

clue.text: Japanese company's refusal to accept plan

indicators.note: to accept means to take the next word inside

parts.note: no is a refusal
to intend is to plan

explanation.surface: A Japanese firm turns down a business proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is the Kyoto-based video game maker.

clue.text: Meal deal (75% off) at the place next to The Bull

indicators.note: removing three quarters of a four-letter word leaves its first letter

parts.words: the place next to The Bull
parts.note: on a target the inner is the ring immediately around the bull's-eye

explanation.surface: A cheap meal offer at a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' looks like a pub name; it is the centre of a dartboard or target, ringed by the INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day.

clue.text: Make pretty amateur blunders with some girl

indicators.note: blunders means the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: An amateur makes mistakes with a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' shuffles A with the letters of SOME GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: To glamorise is to make something more attractive or appealing than it is.

clue.text: Irritation displayed by Hazard when missing header

indicators.note: missing header means without its first letter

parts.note: a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: Eden Hazard, the footballer, shows irritation after a missed header.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazard looks like the Belgian footballer, but is the word for a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong feeling of annoyance, a stronger form of irritation.

clue.text: Lots of people taking off the last bit of their underwear

indicators.note: taking off means removing that letter

parts.note: a throng is a crowd, lots of people

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A crowd stripping off their last item of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' removes R, the last letter of 'their'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy undergarment with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: One learning up front that university's typically extremely expensive

indicators.note: up front means the leading letters of the following words
extremely means the two end letters

explanation.surface: A student told in advance that university is usually very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil being taught by a tutor, a person who is learning.

clue.text: Trendy coastal resort that's in England, not Belgium

indicators.note: not means the letter is taken out

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A fashionable seaside town found in England rather than Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is informal for fashionable or progressive in one's views.

clue.text: Piece of data fraud involving international cryptocurrency

parts.note: a bit is the smallest unit of computer data

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around the next piece

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle

explanation.surface: A data scam with a global reach in the world of digital money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts I inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitcoin is the best-known digital currency secured by cryptography.

clue.text: Willing crazy spenders to cut parts

definitions.note: used as a noun here: a readiness of mind

indicators.note: parts means the jumbled letters separate to take another word inside
crazy means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Persuading reckless shoppers to cut back on parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut parts' reads as reducing components, but 'parts' is the container signal: the jumbled spenders split open to take the word for cut. 'Willing' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparedness is readiness, the state of being willing and ready to act.
